title: school
summary: A familiar place whose word once had a surprising connection to free time.
question: Where did this word come from?
completion: school ← Old English scol ← Latin schola ← Greek skholē. You traced a word through English, Latin and Greek—and discovered a change in meaning as well as spelling. This is the learning word; a school of fish has a different history.
partner: A similar sound is a clue. Let’s check the evidence.

evidence.title: A Latin learning place
evidence.text: Latin schola meant a place of instruction or a learned discussion. English scol came from Latin. But Latin had borrowed this word too.

evidence.title: From leisure to learning
evidence.text: Greek skholē could mean leisure, learned discussion, and a place for lectures. That Greek word gave Latin schola its name. The meanings changed as people used the word in new ways.
